sentences.text: Tajlal Yadav vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 June, 2024

High Court Of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur
 Order Sheet
 Criminal Appeal No.391 of 2021
Tajlal Yadav, son of Shri Ganesh Ram Yadav, aged about 21 years, R/o Village
Mandagaon, Thana Siksod, Civil and Revenue District North Baster Kanker,
Chhattisgarh
 ----- Appellant
 versus
State of Chhattisgarh through the District Magistrate, Kanker, District North Bastar
Kanker, Chhattisgarh
 ----- Respondent
13.6.2024 Shri Sumit Shrivastava, Advocate for the Appellant.
Shri Kanwal Jeet Singh Saini, Panel Lawyer for the State/Respondent.
Shri Jeet Ram Patel, Advocate for the Objector.
Heard on I.A. No.1 of 2024 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.
This is the second application.
First application for suspension of sentence was dismissed as withdrawn on 26.7.2022.

The Appellant has been convicted and sentenced by the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 9.3.2021 passed in Special Criminal Case (POCSO Act) No.13 of 2019 by the Special Judge under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Bhanupratappur, District North Bastar Kanker (Chhattisgarh) as under:
Conviction Sentence Under Section 450 of the R.I. for 3 years and fine of Indian Penal Code Rs.500,
in default of payment of fine, additional R.I. for 6 months Under Section 366 of the R.I. for 3 years and fine of Indian Penal Code Rs.500, in default of payment of fine, additional R.I. for 6 months Under Section 376(2)(i)(n) R.I. for 10 years and fine of of the Indian Penal Code Rs.25,000, in default of payment of fine, additional R.I. for 1 year All the sentences are directed to run concurrently Learned Counsel appearing for the Appellant submits that the Appellant has already suffered 5 years and 1 month out of 10 years of maximum jail sentence awarded to him and the appeal is likely to take some time for hearing on merits.

sentences.text: Considering the fact that the Appellant has suffered 5 years and 1 month out of 10 years of maximum jail sentence awarded to him, the appeal is likely to take some time for hearing on merits and in view of Satender Kumar (supra), I am inclined to allow the application.
Accordingly, I.A. No.1 of 2024 is allowed.

The substantive jail sentence awarded to the Appellant is suspended during the pendency of the instant appeal and he is directed to be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000 (Twenty Five Thousand) with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial Court for his appearance before the Registry of this Court on 31.7.2024.

He shall thereafter appear before the concerned Trial Court on a date to be given by the Registry and he shall continue to appear there on all such subsequent dates as are given to him by the said Court till disposal of this appeal.
It is made clear that the Appellant shall not make any contact with the victim.
List the appeal for final hearing.

It is made clear that the Appellant shall not make any contact with the victim.
List the appeal for final hearing.
